name: CeeLo Green
notes: The research calls this "the most functional harmony in this whole section", and that sentence is what the file is built on: I–vi–IV–V and i–iv–VII–III are authored as the two top families, ii–V–I sits behind them, and `borrowed.V` rises to 0.45 for the secondary dominants the paragraph names — the highest on this axis. `harmonicRhythm` puts `1_per_bar` first because functional motion needs a chord to move on, and `extensions` are 82% coloured (seventh 0.5, ninth 0.32) with `susSubstitutionProb` 0.2 for the gospel suspension. The second thing the paragraph insists on is that this is **a singer's melody, not a rap motif**: `melody.register` spans 57–89, the widest here; `contour.arch` is 0.56; `octaveJumpProb` reaches 0.3; `phraseBars` is the documented 4–8 (with 6 behind them); and `chordToneBias` drops to 0.56 so the line is free to pass between the chord tones rather than spell them. The bass does the opposite — "walking lines and chord-tone targeting" — so its `cellShapes` are replaced with root/3rd/5th/octave shapes and `followRootsProb` sits mid at 0.44. The ad-lib runs out are the outro rule: the countermelody is added there, not dropped, and the section decays. ⚠ **Confidence is medium, and the inferred parameter is the harmony's detail, not its direction.** The research states plainly that his sung role is documented but that "harmonic specifics [are] inferred from the gospel-soul idiom he works in" — so the two named families are the research's, while the exact weights, `borrowed.V` 0.45 and `susSubstitutionProb` 0.2 are INFERRED readings of "secondary dominants" and gospel voice-leading. The tempo band 72–96 is marked [LOW-CONF] in the source; mode 84 is mine. ⛔ **Two things the paragraph asks for are not expressible and are not faked.** There is no pre-chorus section in the engine's vocabulary, so verse/pre-chorus/chorus is authored as the verse–hook pair with the bridge placed before the final hook; and there is no key change, so the "modulation or key lift on the final chorus" is absent rather than approximated. `timbreHint` is `warm_keys` for the organ/Rhodes/choir stack the paragraph names — `church_organ` would have collided with Goodie Mob's, which is the darker end of the same instrument. This model's fill band is `smallEveryBars` 2 / `bigEveryBars` 4 with a 16th/32nd strong-weak roll; inside it, `gapProb` 0.38, `descendProb` 0.49 and the tightest `rampJitter` in the batch at 7 make it the most even-handed fill here, which is what a soul-break roll is. ⚠ **`lockTo808` raised from 0.3 to 0.47.** The 808 takes each kick with this probability, and at 0.3 over this model's 12-kick floor a seed could produce no 808 at all — which `bass808.rs` refuses, because a declared 808 that sometimes vanishes is a part a producer cannot rely on. It is still well under a lock: a good share of kicks carry no sub. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 52 to 46 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 47 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 6. ⚠ `countermelody.fillGapsOnly` returned to true. With it off and a density of 0.72, the counter plays THROUGH the melody rather than around it, and coherence.rs measures that as the counter sounding the melody own pitch at the same moment — a second lead rather than an answer. The register offset and the styles are untouched; what changed is that it waits its turn.
